exposure: Mid-pregnancy psychosocial wellbeing (including care from husband/household, perceived wellbeing, frequency of abuse, affect during third trimester)
Socioeconomic status (including monthly income, husband's education level, use of biomass fuel)
cohort: The study included all third-trimester pregnant women with a singleton pregnancy registered for the national antenatal care programme at Ipalogama health division in Sri Lanka in 2017.
finding: Preterm birth, maternal BMI, and mid-pregnancy psychosocial wellbeing were identified as significant determinants of birthweight, with psychosocial wellbeing being particularly important in a setting where a large proportion of pregnant women experience abuse.
birth_weight: Mean 2912 g (SD 456.6 g), with 14.6% having low birthweight (<2500g) and 9.3% having birthweights > 3500 g.
gest_age: The study included preterm birth as a determinant of birthweight, indicating that babies across different gestational ages at birth were part of the cohort.
